quickAnswer: **Plausible** is the best fit if you want **simple, privacy-respecting web analytics** without GA4 complexity — especially for blogs, marketing sites, and EU-facing properties. Skip it if you need deep ad-platform integration, product funnels, or revenue attribution — **GA4** or **DataFast** cover those better.
bestFor: Marketing sites, blogs, and landing pages that need clean traffic reports without cookie banners in many cases
Teams migrating off Universal Analytics or GA4 for **privacy and simplicity**
Developers who want a **lightweight script** and optional **self-hosting** (open source)
Small businesses comparing privacy-first tools at lower traffic tiers
notFor: Teams deeply invested in Google Ads, BigQuery export, or GA4-native audiences
Product-led SaaS teams needing cohort analysis, session replay, or feature flags
Revenue attribution from Stripe — use **DataFast** or build custom GA4 ecommerce instead
Enterprise analytics with complex governance requirements

sections.title: Privacy & compliance
sections.content:
Plausible is built as a **privacy-first** analytics tool: no cross-site tracking, no personal data sold, and no third-party ad network cookies. It is designed to work **without cookie consent banners** in many EU contexts because it avoids invasive tracking — still verify with legal counsel for your site.

Plausible publishes a **GDPR-compliant DPA** and does not fingerprint users across sites. This is the main reason teams choose it over GA4 for public marketing properties.

Self-hosting gives you full data control on your infrastructure; the managed cloud version keeps ops minimal.

sections.title: Web analytics scope
sections.content:
Plausible covers the essentials well: **pageviews, referrers, UTM campaigns, goals, custom events**, and a realtime dashboard. You get enough to answer "where did traffic come from?" and "which pages convert to signup?" without learning a complex reporting UI.

What you do not get: advanced funnels, user-level product analytics, predictive metrics, or native Google Marketing Platform integrations. For most content and marketing sites, that tradeoff is intentional.

Custom events are supported but keep naming disciplined — each tracked interaction can matter for billing on event-based competitors, though Plausible bills on **pageviews**.

If you already pay for Ahrefs SEO, compare [Ahrefs Web Analytics](/tools/ahrefs/), which is free up to 1M events per project.

sections.title: Cloud vs self-hosted
sections.content:
Most teams use **Plausible Cloud** for speed — add a script tag and go. **Plausible Community Edition (CE)** is the AGPLv3 self-hosted release: twice-yearly long-term releases, community support only, and Cloud premium features (marketing funnels, user journeys, ecommerce revenue goals, SSO, Sites API) omitted. See the [Cloud vs CE table](https://plausible.io/docs/self-hosting) (checked **2026-11-24**).

Self-hosting adds DevOps cost: updates, backups, and uptime are on you. Cloud **Starter** starts at **$9/month for 10K pageviews** on the [homepage](https://plausible.io/) widget (checked **2026-11-24**); CE is free software plus your hosting bill.

setupNotes:
**Typical setup:**

1. Create a site in the Plausible dashboard (or configure self-hosted instance).
2. Add the Plausible script snippet to your site's `<head>` or via your CMS/plugin.
3. Define **goals** for key conversions (signup, download, outbound link clicks).
4. Optionally enable **custom events** for button clicks or JS-tracked actions.

Official plugins exist for WordPress, Ghost, Next.js, and others.

**Common pitfalls:** counting admin/preview traffic (exclude IPs or use filters), forgetting UTM tags on campaigns, and comparing pageview counts 1:1 with GA4 (methodology differs).
pricingNotes:
**Plausible Cloud** prices come from the [homepage](https://plausible.io/) widget (checked **2026-11-24**; `plausible.io/pricing` 404s). **Starter** (one site) is **$9/month at 10k pageviews**, then $19 at 100k, $29 at 200k, $49 at 500k, $69 at 1M, $89 at 2M, **$129 at 5M**, **$169 at 10M**. At 10k pageviews, **Growth is $14/month** (up to 3 sites) and **Business is $19/month**. [Subscription plans](https://plausible.io/docs/subscription-plans) put funnels, user journeys, and revenue tracking on **Business**, not Starter. 30-day trial, no card. Custom events count toward the pageview allowance.

**Plausible CE** has no subscription; you pay for the server. CE omits those Cloud premium features ([self-hosting](https://plausible.io/docs/self-hosting)).

The directory table on this page shows **Starter** amounts. Use our [pricing calculator](/calculators/pricing/) to compare against Fathom and GA4.
limitations: No native Google Ads or Search Console deep integration like GA4.
No session replay, heatmaps, or product analytics — pair with Hotjar or PostHog if needed.
Funnels and advanced segmentation are limited compared with product analytics suites.
Revenue attribution requires custom event work — not built-in like DataFast.
Script performance benchmark pending on AnalyticsVS.

faq.question: Can Plausible replace Google Analytics 4?
faq.answer: For many marketing and content sites, yes — especially when privacy and simplicity matter more than ad-platform integration. GA4 remains stronger for Google Ads attribution and enterprise-scale reporting at no direct cost.

faq.question: Do I need a cookie banner with Plausible?
faq.answer: Plausible is designed to avoid cookies and personal data collection, which often eliminates consent banners in EU contexts. Legal requirements vary — confirm with your counsel.

faq.question: Plausible vs Fathom — how do I choose?
faq.answer: Both are excellent privacy-first options. Plausible tends to be cheaper at very low traffic and offers self-hosting. Fathom emphasizes polished UX and higher entry pageview limits per dollar at some tiers.

faq.question: Is self-hosting worth it?
faq.answer: Only if you have DevOps capacity and a clear data-residency requirement. Most teams should start on cloud and revisit self-hosting if compliance or cost at scale demands it.
